title: sse: fix partial-JSON delimiter ordering and token/event framing in OpenAI-compat streaming
author: Maya Chen
description:
Background: The OpenAI-compat streaming layer occasionally emitted malformed partial-JSON events when response tokens and delimiter events interleaved across TCP chunks, causing downstream clients to drop structured outputs and function/tool-calls. This manifested as: 1) partial JSON fragments arriving without expected delimiter ordering, 2) `token` events and `event` frames being reordered by the framer during chunk boundary handling, and 3) inconsistent handling of trailing commas in partial objects. Motivation: Restore deterministic framing semantics for SSE streaming (OpenAI compat) so structured output and function-calling remains reliable across slow networks and aggressive chunking. Changes in this PR: - Implement a strict delimiter ordering state machine in the SSE framer so delimiters (
, double-newline) are recognized atomically even when split across chunks. - Add token/event coalescing logic: tokens that belong to the same JSON object are buffered until the corresponding delimiter sequence is seen; ordering between token and event frames is preserved. - Normalize how partial JSON commas/trailing braces are emitted so clients receive valid incremental JSON when using partial-json mode. - Update the OpenAI-compat streaming shim to use the framer's atomic-event API instead of ad-hoc newline scanning. - Add unit and integration tests that simulate extreme chunk splits and interleaved token/event sequences. Checklist: - [x] Add framer state machine and tests - [x] Update openai-compat shim to use framer API - [x] Add integration tests that reproduce reported client failures (Linear ENG-1347) - [x] Run cross-language compatibility tests (python/ts/rt) - [x] Add changelog/release note entries Related: Linear ENG-1347, ENG-1399; incident SUP-88. Note: This change is backward compatible for users not relying on previous broken partial-json behavior. Rollout: merged to main; no migration required.

review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Nice state machine - critical to ensure the delimiter atom semantics. One request: add a comment illustrating the expected byte sequences across chunks.
Maya Chen: Added explanatory comments and a small ASCII diagram in sse_framer.rs; also added an integration test that reproduces SUP-88 in the test suite.
Rajesh Kumar: Found a race where a trailing-comma normalization could drop an event if the buffer flushed early. Suggested ensuring flush only on delimiter detection.
Maya Chen: Fixed flush timing to require full delimiter recognition; added unit test for the race case.
Elena García: Approving - ran manual compatibility checks against python and typescript SDKs; structured output and function calls look stable now.
release_notes: Fix SSE streaming partial-JSON and event/token ordering: prevents malformed partial-json frames when chunks split delimiters; improves stability of OpenAI-compat streaming and structured output/function-calling. Backward-compatible.
